description: Every change to an existing guard check rule, with the mandatory pair of tests. A sharpening test covers the newly recognised or newly permitted edge case and fails before the change; a counter test proves the originally repelled violation is still detected and blocked.

changes.summary: The hard deny set gains commit --amend and the comparable local history rewrite operations; detection moves from raw text to parsed arguments.
A mutating request in an undeterminable repository state blocks instead of escalating to ask.
Abstention is stated positively so a crashed guard can no longer be mistaken for a guard without an opinion; the wrapper blocks on anything else.
Targets are extracted per command segment after environment prefixes and wrappers are stripped, so a wrapped or chained mutation no longer hides its target.
Every hook error path blocks; the previous silent exit 0 on missing project directory, missing tooling or missing interpreter is removed.

The interpreter check moves from a path comparison to an ownership check over the whole ancestor chain of the declared and of the actually running interpreter, and the installation root gets the same ancestor check.

When the owner installed guard is both installed and registered on root owned files, the repository side layer abstains instead of deciding. It applies the same rules but cannot see the owner exceptions, so deciding would let a session writable layer veto an owner decision. Without an active authoritative guard the repository layer keeps deciding unchanged.

Detection and redaction now derive from one shared variant source. A flattened user path was previously detected as personal and still written out verbatim; every spelling the detection knows is now redacted by the evidence scrubber and by the guard protocol, or the outgoing evidence is rejected.

Rule R3. Historical acceptance evidence is bound to a committed, PII checked snapshot instead of the gitignored runtime area, and a missing document is a failure instead of a declared not_applicable. A guaranteed to exist artifact must never default to not_applicable, and a hash binding to a volatile, re-runnable file is not durable.

A gate whose acceptance criterion points at a document that does not exist is undefined, not open. It is either re-anchored to a really existing normative source, with the finding proven, or removed from the stage with a reason. A substitute source is never invented.

push and update-ref gain a target bound release. It fires only when the target fully resolves into a throwaway bare repository below a strictly canonicalised, declared fixture root. The real origin, every protected ref, a remote alias resolving onto a protected remote, a symlink that redirects and a parent reference all stay blocked. Unlike an owner exception the release needs no present owner, which is what makes a gate that depends on it reproducible.
changes.violation_set_effect_scope: inside the declared fixture root only; at layer 1 the recognised violation set is unchanged, and every corpus entry stays blocked
changes.owner_decision: Owner decision of 2026-08-06: no guard exception but a target bound rule. An exception needs sudo and expires after 600 seconds; a gate whose run presupposes a present person is not a reproducible gate, and offline-final has to run without the owner.
changes.activation_note: The active installation stays at guard 1.1.0. This change is effective for the guarded session only after the owner reinstalls; no gate depends on that activation.

changes.summary: Rule R4, schema before data. The rule loader gains a declared set of optional fields, so a configuration format can be extended only after its accepting reader knows the field. An undeclared field is still rejected. Enforced generally by a binding of every configuration file to its authoritative reader; a file no reader accepts fails the block.
changes.violation_set_effect_scope: exactly the fields a declared reader accepts; every other unknown field is still rejected
changes.owner_decision: Owner decision of 2026-08-06 establishing rule R4 after the reversed edit order locked the session out: when a configuration format is extended, the accepting reader or validator is effective first, at the latest in the same commit.
changes.finding_origin: Derived from a real finding, not from a hypothesis: adding fixture_targets to rules.json before rules.py knew the field made the repository side guard unable to decide and blocked every tool call. Fail closed worked as designed; the defect was the order.

changes.summary: Rule R6. An expectation value handed to the owner for an owner action must be reproducibly derivable from exactly the commit and the artifact the action refers to, and that derivation belongs to the acceptance evidence. A value carried forward from an earlier derivation is not an expectation value; --expect-hash exists so the owner checks against an independently derived value, not against whatever the installer builds at that moment.
changes.finding_origin: Derived from a real finding: a guard package hash was derived once from an uncommitted worktree state, then published twice for two different commits without being derived again from either. The owner's dry run refused it. Reproduced mechanically — replacing one superseded function in the committed tree reproduces the published value exactly.

declared_relaxations.scope: The declared fixture root .gate-runtime/fixtures/git of the current worktree, and only a throwaway bare repository below it.
still_blocked: the real origin, by name and through any remote alias that resolves onto it
every declared protected ref, wherever it is pushed
a target that leaves the fixture root through a symlink
a target addressed through a symlink inside the fixture root
a path carrying a parent reference
a target that is not a bare repository
a target that is, contains or lies inside the protected repository
any command that is not a single unelevated segment without options
declared_relaxations.owner_decision: Owner decision of 2026-08-06. The two test rule forbids shrinking the violation set only outside declared fixtures; this relaxation lies inside one and is covered by that rule.

fixtures.purpose: Declared corpus for the violation set comparison. Every entry is a synthetic command string; none of them is ever executed.
Guard tests. They run in throwaway temporary installations and never touch the active guard.
Declared PII fixtures. Every value is invented; the real account name is asserted absent at runtime and never written into the file.
Committed, PII checked snapshots of the historical gate evidence. They are data, never re-executed, and bound by hash.

Declared fixture for the target bound release. Every repository lives below a fresh temporary directory; none is ever created inside the protected repository, and the declared root stays relative and below the gitignored runtime area.
Declared binding of every configuration file to its authoritative reader. It binds itself too; rule R4 has no exception for its own declaration.

Declared fixture for rule R6. Every repository is a fresh temporary one built from copies of the guard sources; the protected repository is never committed to, and the two synthetic commits are asserted to really differ so the sharpening test cannot pass on a tie.
